newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH RAILWAY DRUGGER GETS 15 YEARS IN JAIL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH RAILWAY DRUGGER GETS 15 YEARS IN JAIL.

text.p: A robber, whose technique of giving fellow train passengers drug-laced drinks caused the deaths of two people, got a 15-year jail term in a western Poland court on Thursday.
PAP news agency said the Poznan provincial court found the man, dubbed by newspapers the "sleep inducer," had struck twice, in 1991 and 1992. He drugged 26 victims and two died.

The man, identified only as Antoni O., rode around the country amiably offering travel companions vodka mixed with a fizzy drink containing a powerful cocktail of drugs, then stealing from them after they slumped unconscious.
The court sentenced him to 26 terms of six to 15 years in prison but was obliged by Polish law to rule that they should run concurrently, PAP reported.
Judge Pawel Spaleniak said there was no proof that the man meant his victims to die.
The verdict is still open to appeal and under Polish legal custom the surnames of people involved in criminal cases are not revealed.
